extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners learning algebra/arithmetic (historical/Renaissance audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A historical algebra/arithmetic treatise explaining names of quantities, operations on binomials/trinomials, rules for forming and reducing equations, and canonical procedures (canons) for manipulation and root extraction. Contains definitions, worked examples, and algorithmic prescriptions for multiplying, reducing, equating, and transforming algebraic quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for multiplying polynomials (trinomial × terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise algorithm to multiply a trinomial by other terms: multiply the trinomial by a given term, record the remainder, and continue multiplying and reducing term-by-term until the product is obtained (eventually reducing to a single folio / term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: passages describe taking 'il trinomio poi multiplicaro a ino ...' and working 'mano ì mano facido' so that 'observando le pjadate regole virra lo tuo effetto oc riasfeuna omifione benifTimo oe qualuncbe quantia fi voglia.' Examples: multiply a trinomial by successive names, form remainders and continue (the text walks through multiplying, forming remainders, and repeating until one folio/result). Anti-pattern: multiplying out of sequence or ignoring remainders will fail to produce the correct consolidated product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing a trinomial via its remainder ('recifo' / 'recifo trinomiale')
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trinomial is multiplied and produces leftover terms, form its 'recifo' (remainder) and use it in the subsequent multiplication steps until the expression is reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly uses 'recifo'/'recifo trinomiale' and prescribes carrying forward the remainder into the next operation (e.g., 'ptèdolo p lo trinomio neaiira el fuo recifo'). Guidance shows numeric examples and the iterative nature of reducing by successive remainders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mediation to order terms when multiplying (placing the mean term)
rubrics_metrics.description: When arranging terms for multiplication (especially with differing magnitudes), put the term that is 'piu o meno' (more or less) in the middle (mediate) to facilitate proper multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'mediate el terni io piu ouer DiTgióro mediate el tehnìo 6l meno ... il piu o il meno metti el meiio.' The guidance gives a procedural ordering heuristic: choose the middle term appropriately to multiply extremes and middle terms systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated multiplication proportional to the unit count
rubrics_metrics.description: To multiply a quantity by another a number of times, multiply the quantity as many times as there are units and then combine/reduce the results accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrasing: 'recojdati ràre volte ^te tu mebi el mulnnomio: c per le medefi^ me ^^t3^e volte multiplica la quantità che tu oouiui ptireXómo lei tuo prit02e fofie.' Examples in the text show multiplying by 2, 3, 4 etc., and then reducing via combination of like terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: When terms equal a number: reduce the whole equation by dividing through the number
rubrics_metrics.description: If the terms (le cofe) and the 'cenfi' (units/powers) are equal to a number, reduce the entire equation by that number (divide all terms by that number) to simplify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: 'Quando li cenfi e le cofe fe aguagliano al numero... ridurc laequanb ne tutta.a.vn cenfotcioc fe ci fia manco de.' The guidance prescribes dividing the whole equation by the given number (or subtracting/moving terms) so the equation becomes simpler; examples illustrate dividing when a common numerical value appears on both sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when things (cofe) equal numbers: move/partition and value accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: If quantities are equal to numbers, one may 'partire el tornerò' or reassign which is first/second in accounting for the unit and value, while remaining attentive to the doctrine about ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrasing: 'Quando le cofe firanno equali al numero* Blo2a fe die partire el tornerò per le cofe e la uenimcnto fia numero c Valuta dclacofa.' Guidance: be careful with which term is taken as the primary unit; ordering conventions affect reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical rules for equating and reducing to a common power (canonici / 'canonia')
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of canonical rules (first, second, third canons) for transforming quantities when extracting roots, comparing products, and reducing forms (e.g., handling square root, square of a product, and median/root operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headings: 'ladini canonioverfuo', 'Secundi canonia verfuo.', 'Terti canonia verfua.' Examples: first canon: reduce a number to its root; second canon: product of a square gives square root; third canon: operations involving radices and combining superstructures. The text lists procedural rules to accept, reduce, or recombine roots and squares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and identification of square (quadrato), cube (cubo), and other powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Square (quadrato) is the product of a quantity by itself; cube is the product of the quantity by its square; these names indicate how quantities behave under multiplication and help to classify terms in equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrasing: 'il quadrato... ogni numero ... multiplicato in fe medefima fia quadrato ... come nel principio De lope' and 'cubo ... relatiò.' Guidance shows how to interpret algebraic names geometrically and arithmetically; examples map geometric area (square) to arithmetic square and relate numbers like 4, 16, 64 to powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming and treating quantities: units, determinate numbers, and their roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers and quantities are to be considered with their units; one must distinguish a determinate (determinated) number and the unit associated, and name quantities accordingly for algebraic operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text explains 'Dico numero ertereC fecondo ebe... ogni quantità porta Tempre feco el Tuo Determinato nis mero' and stresses that naming (denominare) quantities supports correct algebraic manipulation. Guidance: keep track of units and names to avoid confusion in operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of equality and comparison between terms and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple modes by which quantities can be equal to one another (one-to-one, two-to-one, etc.), and the treatise catalogs these modes and their implications for manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original: '£>23 e da vedere in quanri modi fralo20 fe polla Inno a laltro:c laltro a luno.£ li doi a luno,£ Innoa li doi.aguagliare.' Guidance: the enumeration of equality types informs which algebraic transformations (equating, substituting) are permissible; the text also introduces terms like 'simple', 'composite', 'compositione' for categorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for combining like terms and inability to combine unlike powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Only quantities of the same kind/degree (same 'dignità' — e.g., both squares, both cubes, or same unit) can be combined; differing powers cannot be added directly and must be reduced to a common measure first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrasing: 'fe altra Dignità 0 vero ... in Die ta equatione magioie De céforedmo cubo 0 cenfo dc cèfo.' Guidance: examples demonstrate combining terms of same degree and warn against combining unlike terms without transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to a common denomination (reducing to the same unit/power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform multiple terms to a common denomination (e.g., reduce all to squares, cubes, or to the unit) to perform comparisons and simplifications; often by multiplying/dividing to achieve matching powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'cofi qnido Diccmo la.i.Dc vn qdrato ouer De. 1 .ce.e iguali...' and many numerical examples (powers of 2: 4,16,64...) show converting between denominations. Guidance: this is the method to collect all like items before equating or reducing the equation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dividing an equation by a common factor / reducing coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: If all terms of an equation share a common numerical factor, divide the entire equation by that factor to reduce coefficients and simplify the equation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages describe dividing by 'la mea' or a common number ('quale ... dividendo tutto la eqtioe ... partila tutta nella $".dc li cefi'). Example: when each term has factor 2, divide through by 2 to reduce to simpler integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling irregular cases when quantities equate to quantities ('De obferuantia iiiregulariu')
rubrics_metrics.description: Special attention is required when terms on both sides equate in a non-regular way (e.g., different counts on each side, or asymmetrical contributions); such irregular equalities have their own prescribed treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 'De obferuantia iiiregulariu' explains how to handle cases where 'le cofe fe agiiagliano a cofe' but values distributed unequally; guidance prescribes identifying the objective value sought and reorganizing the terms to conclude the desired equality by accounting the differential contributions and using examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worked exemplars as a method for verification (exempla: semplici, compositi, composti)
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatise furnishes worked examples in categories — simple (semplici), composite (composti), mixed — to illustrate canonical procedures and verify rules in concrete numeric cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections 'De evemplis trium fimpliciu' and 'De eeèplis trìu capituloju còpofito' give step-by-step examples: multiply a number by 4, square it, reduce, etc., showing how to apply the algorithms. Guidance: use these exemplars to test understanding and confirm procedural correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic–geometric correspondence: interpret algebraic terms via geometry (squares/areas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate algebraic names (square, side length, area) to geometric figures: a square's surface corresponds to the square of its side, enabling geometric intuition for algebraic powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrasing: 'la fupficie dc vn quadrato... la fupficie fira.4.rne.*^.£ cofi la Aia...' Guidance: map algebraic operations to geometric constructions when reasoning about powers and proportionalities; the text uses polygonal area examples to justify algebraic equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalogue of regular equality types and canonical classifications (simple, compound, composite equalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify equalities into regular sorts — simple (semplici), complex/composite (compofl:i), and composed relations — and follow the rules appropriate to each class when manipulating equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text lists classifications: 'femplicic.5.compofl:i.' and prescribes how regular equalities behave under algebraic operations, including which transformations preserve equality and how to reduce to canonical forms.
